points.title: 早年成长
points.description: 米尔顿·弗里德曼1912年7月31日出生于纽约布鲁克林的一个犹太移民家庭。他的父母来自奥匈帝国，父亲经营服装厂。弗里德曼在布鲁克林长大，在拉比亚伯拉罕·卡普兰学校接受早期教育。这段时期他展现出对数学和科学的浓厚兴趣，为日后成为经济学家奠定了基础。家庭环境强调教育和自我提升，这对弗里德曼后来的学术取向产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: Milton Friedman was born on July 31, 1912, in Brooklyn, New York, to Jewish immigrant parents from Austria-Hungary. His father worked in a clothing factory. Friedman grew up in Brooklyn and received his early education at Rabbi Abraham Kaplan School. During this period, he developed a strong interest in mathematics and science, which laid the foundation for his future career as an economist. His family emphasized education and self-improvement, which profoundly influenced his later academic orientation.

points.place: 美国新泽西州拉特格斯大学
points.placeEn: Rutgers University, New Jersey, United States
points.title: 大学启蒙
points.description: 弗里德曼进入拉特格斯大学学习，最初主修数学，后转向经济学。在拉特格斯，他遇到了影响他一生的经济学教授阿瑟·伯恩斯，后来成为美联储主席。伯恩斯引导弗里德曼对经济学产生浓厚兴趣，并培养了他对实证研究的重视。弗里德曼在大学期间展现出卓越的学术能力，获得经济学奖学金，并于1932年获得学士学位。这段经历确立了他对经济学的终身追求，并开始形成他对自由市场经济的早期理解。
points.descriptionEn: Friedman attended Rutgers University, initially majoring in mathematics before switching to economics. At Rutgers, he met Arthur Burns, who would later become Chairman of the Federal Reserve, and who profoundly influenced Friedman's interest in economics. Burns introduced Friedman to the importance of empirical research. Friedman demonstrated exceptional academic ability, receiving scholarships in economics, and graduated with a bachelor's degree in 1932. This period solidified his lifelong pursuit of economics and began forming his early understanding of free-market principles.

points.placeEn: University of Chicago, Illinois, United States
points.title: 学术深造
points.description: 弗里德曼进入芝加哥大学攻读经济学硕士学位，师从著名经济学家亨利·西蒙斯和弗兰克·奈特。在这里，他接触到自由市场理论，形成了对政府干预的怀疑态度。1933年，弗里德曼获得芝加哥大学硕士学位，随后前往哥伦比亚大学继续深造。在芝加哥大学的短暂学习经历对他产生了深远影响，为他后来成为芝加哥学派的核心人物奠定了基础。他开始系统研究货币理论，这将成为他日后学术贡献的核心领域。
points.descriptionEn: Friedman entered the University of Chicago for graduate studies in economics, studying under renowned economists Henry Simons and Frank Knight. Here, he was exposed to free-market theories and developed skepticism toward government intervention. In 1933, Friedman received his master's degree from Chicago before moving to Columbia University for further studies. His brief time at Chicago profoundly influenced him, laying the foundation for his later role as a leading figure in the Chicago School. He began systematically studying monetary theory, which would become the core of his future academic contributions.

points.placeEn: University of Chicago, Illinois, United States
points.title: 学术巅峰
points.description: 1946年，弗里德曼重返芝加哥大学任教，开始了长达30年的学术生涯。在这里，他与乔治·斯蒂格勒、阿诺德·哈伯格等人共同发展了芝加哥学派经济学。弗里德曼在这一时期完成了他最具影响力的学术工作，包括1953年发表的《实证经济学方法论》，1963年与安娜·施瓦茨合著的《美国货币史（1867-1960）》，以及1968年提出的自然失业率假说。他还为《新闻周刊》撰写专栏，将经济学思想普及给大众。1976年，弗里德曼因其在消费分析、货币历史和理论以及稳定政策复杂性方面的贡献获得诺贝尔经济学奖。芝加哥时期是弗里德曼学术成就最辉煌的阶段，他彻底改变了宏观经济学的面貌。
points.descriptionEn: In 1946, Friedman returned to the University of Chicago to teach, beginning a 30-year academic career. Here, he developed the Chicago School of economics with colleagues like George Stigler and Arnold Harberger. During this period, Friedman completed his most influential academic work, including 'The Methodology of Positive Economics' (1953), 'A Monetary History of the United States, 1867-1960' (1963) with Anna Schwartz, and his natural rate hypothesis (1968). He also wrote columns for Newsweek, popularizing economic ideas among the public. In 1976, Friedman received the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for his achievements in consumption analysis, monetary history and theory, and the complexity of stabilization policy. The Chicago period represented the pinnacle of Friedman's academic achievements, fundamentally transforming macroeconomics.

points.title: 政策影响
points.description: 弗里德曼在1964年担任巴里·戈德华特总统竞选的经济顾问，正式进入政策领域。1969-1971年，他担任理查德·尼克松总统的经济顾问委员会成员，尽管他对尼克松的价格管制政策持批评态度。弗里德曼的思想对1970年代和1980年代的经济政策产生了深远影响，特别是通过他与玛格丽特·撒切尔和罗纳德·里根的密切关系。他倡导的自由市场理念、货币主义政策和减少政府干预的主张成为里根政府经济政策的理论基础。在华盛顿的经历使弗里德曼从学者转变为政策影响者，他的思想直接影响了西方国家的经济政策方向。
points.descriptionEn: Friedman served as an economic advisor to Barry Goldwater's presidential campaign in 1964, formally entering the policy arena. From 1969 to 1971, he was a member of President Richard Nixon's Council of Economic Advisers, though he criticized Nixon's price control policies. Friedman's ideas profoundly influenced economic policy in the 1970s and 1980s, particularly through his close relationships with Margaret Thatcher and Ronald Reagan. His advocacy for free-market principles, monetarist policies, and reduced government intervention became the theoretical foundation for Reagan's economic policies. His Washington experience transformed Friedman from an academic into a policy influencer, with his ideas directly shaping the direction of Western economic policy.

points.place: 美国加利福尼亚州旧金山
points.title: 晚年影响
points.description: 1977年，弗里德曼离开芝加哥大学，加入斯坦福大学胡佛研究所，继续他的学术工作。他与妻子罗丝·弗里德曼共同创作了《自由选择》(1980)一书，并制作了同名电视系列片，进一步推广了自由市场理念。1988年，里根总统授予弗里德曼总统自由勋章。晚年，弗里德曼继续通过写作、演讲和媒体参与公共辩论，捍卫自由市场原则。他成为全球自由市场经济学的标志性人物，影响了无数政策制定者和学者。2006年11月16日，弗里德曼在旧金山家中去世，享年94岁。他的思想遗产继续影响着全球经济政策讨论，特别是在金融危机后关于政府角色的辩论中。
points.descriptionEn: In 1977, Friedman left the University of Chicago to join the Hoover Institution at Stanford University, continuing his academic work. With his wife Rose Friedman, he authored 'Free to Choose' (1980) and produced a同名 television series, further promoting free-market principles. In 1988, President Reagan awarded Friedman the Presidential Medal of Freedom. In his later years, Friedman continued to participate in public debates through writing, speaking, and media appearances, defending free-market principles. He became an iconic figure of global free-market economics, influencing countless policymakers and scholars. Friedman died on November 16, 2006, at his home in San Francisco at age 94. His intellectual legacy continues to influence global economic policy discussions, particularly in debates about government's role following financial crises.

supporter.zh: 弗里德曼被誉为20世纪最具影响力的经济学家之一，他通过货币主义理论和自由市场理念重塑了现代经济学。支持者认为他成功挑战了凯恩斯主义的主导地位，为全球范围内的经济自由化提供了理论基础。他的政策建议帮助许多国家摆脱滞胀困境，促进了经济增长。弗里德曼强调个人自由与市场效率的关系，主张有限政府，这些思想成为现代保守主义和自由意志主义的核心。他的教育普及工作使经济学思想超越了学术界，影响了普通民众的思考方式。
supporter.en: Friedman is regarded as one of the most influential economists of the 20th century, who reshaped modern economics through monetarist theory and free-market principles. Supporters believe he successfully challenged the dominance of Keynesian economics and provided the theoretical foundation for economic liberalization worldwide. His policy recommendations helped many countries escape stagflation and promoted economic growth. Friedman emphasized the relationship between individual freedom and market efficiency, advocating for limited government—ideas that became central to modern conservatism and libertarianism. His educational work brought economic ideas beyond academia, influencing how ordinary people think about economic issues.

critic.zh: 批评者认为弗里德曼的经济思想过于简化复杂的社会现实，过度强调市场机制而忽视市场失灵。他的货币主义政策在实践中的效果受到质疑，特别是在2008年金融危机后，放松监管的后果显而易见。批评者指出，弗里德曼对大企业的态度过于宽容，未能充分关注财富不平等问题。他的教育市场化理念被批评为可能导致教育质量下降和社会分层加剧。此外，弗里德曼在智利军政府时期提供的政策建议也引发争议，被指责为支持威权政权。
critic.en: Critics argue that Friedman's economic thoughts oversimplify complex social realities and overemphasize market mechanisms while ignoring market failures. The effectiveness of his monetarist policies in practice has been questioned, particularly after the 2008 financial crisis, when the consequences of deregulation became evident. Critics point out that Friedman's attitude toward large corporations was too tolerant, and he failed to adequately address wealth inequality. His ideas about market-based education have been criticized for potentially leading to decreased educational quality and increased social stratification. Additionally, Friedman's policy advice to the Chilean military government has been controversial, with accusations of supporting authoritarian regimes.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，弗里德曼被定义为20世纪经济思想变革的关键人物。他代表了从国家干预向市场导向的重大转变，这一转变重塑了全球政治经济格局。弗里德曼的思想超越了传统意识形态界限，影响了从左到右的各类政治人物。他的著作和电视节目使经济学变得平易近人，扩大了公共讨论的范围。尽管他的政策建议存在争议，但弗里德曼对经济学方法论和实证研究的贡献被广泛认可。在流行文化中，他常被描绘为自由市场的捍卫者，其形象成为经济自由主义的象征。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Friedman is defined as a key figure in the transformation of economic thought in the 20th century. He represented a major shift from state intervention to market orientation that reshaped the global political economy. Friedman's ideas transcended traditional ideological boundaries, influencing political figures across the spectrum. His writings and television programs made economics accessible to the public, expanding the scope of public discourse. While his policy recommendations remain controversial, his contributions to economic methodology and empirical research are widely recognized. In popular culture, he is often portrayed as a defender of free markets, becoming an icon of economic liberalism.

self.zh: 一个社会的自由程度可以用两个指标来衡量：一是政府支出占国民生产总值的比例，二是政府雇员占总人口的比例。
self.en: The degree of freedom in a society can be measured by two indicators: the proportion of government spending to GNP and the proportion of government employees to the total population.

others.zh: 米尔顿·弗里德曼是20世纪后半叶最具影响力的经济学家，他重新塑造了人们对政府在经济中角色的理解。
others.en: Milton Friedman was the most influential economist of the second half of the 20th century; he reshaped people's understanding of the role of government in the economy.
